Call us at 8308103366 or Chat on WhatsApp . 10 modules Statistics to Generative AI 5 months Weekday, weekend and fast-track batches 21 projects Including 2 capstone projects Beginner friendly No coding background needed 2 certificates Course completion and internship About Syllabus Projects Trainer Batches & fees Careers Reviews Locations FAQs Enroll now About this data science course This course is for people in Pune who want a job in data, not just another certificate. You start with the basics that every analyst needs (statistics, Excel and SQL), move on to Python and machine learning, and finish with deep learning, Generative AI and Power BI dashboards. Every module ends with hands-on work on real datasets. By the last month you will have a GitHub portfolio of projects you can open in an interview and explain line by line. You can take the same course in a classroom at one of our three Pune branches, live online from anywhere in India, or as a hybrid where you learn online and do project work on campus. You don’t need a coding or maths background. A typical batch mixes fresh graduates, working professionals switching careers, and people restarting after a break. The trainer starts from the fundamentals and reviews your code as you go, so nobody gets left behind. What you’ll learn Clean, explore and analyse real datasets with Python, Pandas, NumPy and SQL Build, test and tune machine learning models, from linear regression to random forests and XGBoost Train neural networks for images, text and time-series data Turn raw data into Power BI dashboards a manager can actually use Use ChatGPT, Claude and prompt engineering to speed up everyday data work Explain your projects with confidence in interviews and case-study rounds Certificates Course completion and internship certificate Ways to learn Classroom, live online or hybrid Support 24x7 doubt support and lifetime access to study material Payment EMI available at 0% interest Skills you’ll gain Python SQL and MySQL Statistics Probability MS Excel Pandas NumPy Matplotlib Seaborn SciPy Exploratory data analysis Feature engineering Machine learning Scikit-learn XGBoost Deep learning NLP Time-series forecasting Generative AI Prompt engineering Power BI Power Query Tableau Git and GitHub Who this course is for Anyone who is a graduate, a postgraduate, a college student or a working professional can join. Knowing some Python, SQL or statistics helps, but it is not required, because we teach all of it from the start. Fresh graduates You want your first job as a data analyst or data scientist and need real projects to talk about in interviews. Working professionals You work in IT, finance, sales or operations and want to move into a data role without quitting your job. Evening and weekend batches fit around work. Non-IT backgrounds You come from commerce, arts, mechanical or another field. We start with Excel and basic statistics before any code. Career restarters You have a career gap and want an up-to-date, practical skill set and help getting back into interviews. Final-year students You want to graduate with a portfolio and an internship certificate, not just a degree. Not sure yet? Read our guide to data science course eligibility after 12th and graduation , or book a free demo class. How you’ll learn Theory is kept short. Each concept is explained, practised in a lab, and then used in a project before you move on. Stage What the trainer does What you get Concept building Explains statistics, ML basics and data science ideas with examples from real businesses A solid analytical foundation Hands-on labs Walks you through Python notebooks, SQL queries, EDA and model building, step by step Practical, tool-based skills Assignments and projects Reviews your code, points out mistakes, and runs business case studies in ML, analytics and dashboards Project experience employers ask about Interview preparation Runs ML questions, case studies and mock interviews Confidence for data science hiring rounds Syllabus 2026 Data science course syllabus: 10 modules The syllabus works for complete beginners and for working professionals. Each module builds on the one before it. Select a module to see what it covers. Module 1: Statistics and data science fundamentals The maths you actually need, explained with examples before formulas. Data science basics What data science is and why companies need it, big data, how data science relates to machine learning, the data science life cycle, platforms, real use cases and the skills a data scientist needs. Mathematics for data science Linear algebra and matrices: zero, one, identity, diagonal, column and row matrices, and matrix operations. Statistics Structured and unstructured data, measures of central tendency and dispersion, the empirical rule, confidence intervals and the central limit theorem. Probability and distributions Probability theory, conditional probability, data distributions, and normal and binomial distributions. Hypothesis testing Large vs small sample tests, one-sample z-test, one- and two-sample t-tests, testing population means, and the chi-square test. Module 2: MS Excel for analysis Still the quickest way to check data in most offices, so we make sure you are fluent. Working with spreadsheets Ranges and selection, fill and sequences, adding and moving cells, formulas, and relative vs absolute references. Everyday functions SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, MIN, RANDBETWEEN, TRIM, LEN, CONCATENATE, TODAY and NOW. Logical functions IF, IF with calculations, COUNTIF and COUNTIFS. Charts Visualising data with charts, chart elements and styles, data labels and quick layouts. Module 3: SQL and relational databases Querying, joining and summarising data, the skill almost every data job in Pune asks for. RDBMS and data retrieval Introduction to RDBMS and SQL, retrieving data, wildcard pattern matching and sorting with ORDER BY. Aggregation and joins Aggregate functions, GROUP BY, HAVING, nested queries, and inner, multi and outer joins. Changing tables Adding and deleting columns, renaming columns and changing data types, creating tables from existing tables, and foreign key constraints. Module 4: Python for data science From your first line of Python to analysing data with NumPy, Pandas and Matplotlib. Python basics Why Python, setting up the environment, identifiers and keywords. Control flow and files Data types and variables, conditions and loops, decorators, and working with files and directories. Core objects and functions Strings, lists, dictionaries and tuples, built-in functions and writing your own functions. NumPy Array operations and functions, mean, standard deviation, max and min, reshaping and resizing, random functions and transpose. Pandas Series and DataFrames, selecting and retrieving data, describe and info, pivoting, and combining data with merge and concatenation. Matplotlib Basic plots and containers, components and properties, scatter plots, histograms, bar and pie charts, and box plots. SciPy Hypothesis testing with SciPy: Shapiro, Spearman, independent t-test and chi-square. Want more Python first? See our Python training in Pune . Module 5: Machine learning Preparing data, building models, and knowing whether a model is actually any good. Exploratory data analysis Exploring data, handling missing values and outliers, feature engineering, train-test split, standard and min-max scaling, pre-processing, and up- and down-sampling. Supervised learning Linear regression, R² and adjusted R², MSE and RMSE, gradient descent and logistic regression. Model evaluation and more algorithms Accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, confusion matrix, classification report, k-fold cross-validation, ROC and AUC, k-nearest neighbours, decision trees, random forest, support vector machines and hyperparameter tuning. Unsupervised learning Similarity measures, k-means clustering and the elbow method. Ensembles and dimensionality reduction Bagging, boosting and principal component analysis. Module 6: Artificial intelligence and deep learning Neural networks for text, images and time-series data. AI foundations What AI is, its history, and where the market is heading. Natural language processing Tokenisation, part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, semantic analysis and sentiment analysis. Artificial neural networks How ANNs work, ReLU and softmax activations, and building and evaluating an ANN. Convolutional neural networks Convolution and filtering, padding, max pooling, dense layers, and building and evaluating a CNN. Recurrent neural networks How RNNs work, building and evaluating an RNN, and LSTM. Time-series data Cleaning and pre-processing time-series data, and forecasting with LSTM and ARIMA. Module 7: Generative AI How large language models work and how to use them well in real data work. Foundations of AI How AI evolved from the 1950s to today, including the Turing Test and Deep Blue; ML, deep learning, neural networks, perceptrons and transformers such as BERT and GPT; narrow, general and superintelligent AI; and real applications in customer service, marketing and finance. Introduction to Generative AI What Generative AI is, how it differs from traditional AI, large language models, and how GPT, Gemini and Claude compare. Prompt engineering and task automation Prompt structure (context, task, output), zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, ReAct and role-based prompting, common mistakes and how to fix them, reusable prompt templates, and hands-on task automation with ChatGPT and Claude. Related course: Generative AI course in Pune . Module 8: Git and GitHub Version control, so your projects live in a portfolio recruiters can see. Introduction to Git and distributed version control, the Git life cycle, clone and commit, push and update, and stash, move, rename and delete operations. Module 9: Data visualisation with Power BI From connecting to data to publishing a dashboard people can use. Getting started with Power BI Why businesses need BI, Power BI Desktop, Service and Mobile, Report Builder vs paginated reports, installation, the interface, and data sources such as Excel, CSV, SQL Server, web APIs, Azure, SharePoint, OneDrive and folders. Loading and transforming data with Power Query Import vs DirectQuery; splitting, merging and renaming columns; changing data types; column from examples; filtering, sorting and grouping rows; handling missing values; removing duplicates; pivot and unpivot; and conditional columns. Visuals and dashboards Bar, line, pie and donut charts, matrix and table visuals, cards, maps, slicers and filters, synced slicers, drill-down and drill-through, tooltips, formatting and custom themes. Related course: Power BI course in Pune . Module 10: Projects and case studies Machine learning, deep learning and Power BI projects, two capstones, and industry case studies. This is where everything comes together. See the full list of projects you’ll build . Syllabus updated October 2026. Module content is reviewed as tools and hiring needs change, so your batch may include newer topics. Projects you’ll build You will work on 21 real-time projects during the course. Every project goes on your GitHub, and the trainer reviews your code before it does. Here is a selection. Machine learning Profit prediction for startups with multiple linear regression Diabetes, pre-diabetes and non-diabetes classification with multiclass logistic regression Spam mail detection with gradient boosting, XGBoost and random forest Drug classification with k-nearest neighbours Loan defaulter classification with SVM Customer grouping with k-means and agglomerative clustering Product associations with association rule mining Deep learning and AI Power plant energy prediction with an ANN CIFAR-10 image classification with a CNN Handwritten digit classification with a CNN IMDB movie review sentiment analysis with an RNN Air passenger forecasting with ARIMA Next-word generator with NLP and LSTM Power BI dashboards Retail sales dashboard: sales vs target KPIs, category and region breakdown HR analytics dashboard: attrition, hiring trends, department analysis Financial performance report: P&L view, trends and year-on-year comparison Supply chain and inventory dashboard: stock levels and supplier performance Capstone projects Delivery duration prediction Predict how long an order will take to arrive, from raw data to a tested model. Machine failure prediction Predict equipment failure early, so parts can be replaced before a breakdown. Industry case studies These case studies follow a real project from data collection to cloud deployment, including how to choose features and models, how much data is enough, and how CI/CD works in a data project. Domain The business problem What you practise Insurance Decide a client’s premium from their profile, to keep existing clients and win new ones Feature selection, model choice, CI/CD and cloud deployment Healthcare imaging Help a hospital detect pneumonia in chest X-rays automatically Image pre-processing and augmentation, transfer learning, incremental learning HR and NLP Assess a job applicant’s level of English communication Text representation and pre-processing, transfer learning for text Manufacturing Predictive maintenance of engine parts, so they are replaced before a machine fails Time-series pre-processing and ML/DL models for time-series data Sales Forecast product demand so the company can plan stock and staff Time-series forecasting and deployment Tools you’ll use You practise every tool on real datasets, in the same environments data teams use: Jupyter Notebook, Google Colab and GitHub. MySQL NumPy Power BI Tableau MS Excel ChatGPT Also covered: Python, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, SciPy, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow and Keras, Power Query, Git and Claude. They teach the way data work is actually done in companies: how a project goes from data collection to deployment, how data scientists work with engineering and business teams, and which skills matter most for entry and mid-level roles. They have guided hundreds of learners from non-tech backgrounds, and they are good at explaining hard ideas simply. They don’t just prepare you for a certificate.
